cells.tense: You're working it out as you go, and that's exactly the right speed.
cells.verb: seeing the shape in things before they're finished
cells.place: in the stretch where nothing is settled yet
cells.ask: Bring one thing you've worked out to someone who's also in the dark about it, and let yourself feel what's between you as much as what's figured out. What comes back is closeness that leaves both of you whole.
cells.core:
You're working it out as you go, and that's exactly the right speed. You can see the shape in things before they're finished — the pattern shows up in the half-light and you don't demand more light than you've got. One step reads clearly, then the next. The logic holds without needing the whole road.
That's rare, and it's free to feed something: the people who are in the dark alongside you. You've been doing the seeing on your own. It doesn't have to stay private.
cells.sheetLine: You read the pattern one step at a time, and that's enough light.

cells.tense: You're solving a future that hasn't shown up yet.
cells.verb: running every unknown through the mind until it's a diagram
cells.place: in the stretch where nothing is settled yet
cells.ask: Pick one next step, call it decided, and let the rest stay uncomputed for a day. What comes back is a kind of seeing that opens doors instead of boarding them up.
cells.core:
You're solving a future that hasn't shown up yet. Every unknown gets run through the mind until it's a diagram — branches, odds, contingencies — and the not-knowing never gets a chance to just be not-knowing. The pattern-seeing that usually serves you has started working overtime on roads you haven't reached.
What's missing isn't more analysis. It's a decision that stands. One clear next step, held firm, does what a hundred scenarios can't: it gives the mind somewhere to rest.
cells.sheetLine: You're mapping roads you haven't reached yet.

cells.tense: Somewhere back there, you stopped trying to make sense of it.
cells.place: in the stretch where nothing is settled yet
cells.ask: Go toward someone walking a road like yours and let their way of making sense sit beside you for a while — not to adopt it, just to be near it. What comes back is your own seeing, the kind that frees rather than pins.
cells.core:
Somewhere back there, you stopped trying to make sense of it. The fog came in, the mind said it can't see, and it quit looking — so now you're moving through the uncertainty with no reading of it at all, taking steps without noticing what they're telling you. The capacity didn't leave. It went quiet.
Forcing yourself to think harder won't restart it. What tends to is company: being near how someone else makes meaning of a hard stretch. Understanding is contagious when you stand close enough.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped reading the pattern, and you're still in the fog.

cells.tense: You've already worked out where this is heading, and you're calling it a hunch.
cells.verb: seeing the pattern and not claiming it
cells.place: in the stretch where nothing is settled yet
cells.ask: Say what you already see, out loud, and then notice what you feel about having seen it — the pull toward it or away. What comes back is understanding you can stand behind, and room for whoever else is in the picture.
cells.core:
You've already worked out where this is heading, and you're calling it a hunch. The pattern is clear to you — you can feel yourself acting on it, choosing around it — but you talk about it as if the fog were still thick. The seeing happened. The owning didn't.
The way back isn't more thinking; the thinking's done. It's noticing what you feel about what you figured out. Once the seeing has a feeling attached, it's hard to keep pretending it isn't yours.
cells.sheetLine: You've already seen the shape. You're still calling it a guess.
